FROM NATIVE LOGS TO EXPLICIT ASSISTANCE EVIDENCE

Use existing logs.
Keep the limits.

We built QLM Measure to measure AI scaffolding, then defined Learnlog as the capture agreement for our products. We are preparing the transformer for open release so other products can keep their native logs. Source-specific adapters translate supported exports into Learnlog while preserving gaps and unknowns.

External vendors do not need to implement a new Learnlog format. Each source needs a documented mapping; translation cannot recover help nobody logged.

THE CONTRIBUTION IS THE AGREEMENT
Use xAPI and Caliper.
Specify the assistance rules.
xAPI Profiles support domain concepts, extensions, statement rules and patterns. Caliper defines learning-event models and metric profiles. Learnlog uses these extension mechanisms for a particular assistance capture agreement; a valid base event alone does not establish that agreement.

        
Existing mechanisms and the proposed Learnlog agreement
Measurement questionExisting mechanismsProposed Learnlog agreement
Which assistance stage occurred?Domain vocabularies, event types, profiles and extensions can describe stages.Define the observation trigger for each lifecycle stage. A request never stands in for a display.
What could the instrument observe?Event context and extensions can carry instrumentation information.Declare capabilities, boundaries, observation windows and coverage before interpreting an absent event.
What remains unknown, and why?Profiles and extensions can carry knowledge states and provenance.Distinguish not collected, not reported and not reviewed; retain evidence for observed claims. Missing never silently becomes zero.

        
Related AI and intelligent-tutoring work already exists, including the draft AI-Mediated Learning Interactions Profile with AI-scaffold requests and responses, and GIFT’s xAPI statements. Learnlog proposes a particular joint contract for capture boundaries, achieved coverage, typed unknowns and evidence provenance. It is not a claim that existing standards lack the expressive power, lack AI assistance vocabularies or that no related profile exists. This comparison concerns the base mechanisms, not an exhaustive audit of every domain profile. The same agreement can be supported through existing logging ecosystems.

        
Keep native logs.
Make the mapping explicit.
Existing products can contribute supported exports through an adapter instead of emitting a new format. A retrospective transformer can preserve existing evidence and expose gaps; it cannot reconstruct events nobody logged. Prospective instrumentation can capture missing context. Shared rules make interpretation inspectable. Their effect on research errors or effort still needs independent evaluation.

What the shared count cannot establish
The total number of requests that actually occurred, cross-source learner identities, comparable request rates, help displayed, reading and learning remain unestablished. Adding another source increases the recorded evidence; it does not establish a shared population or equivalent exposure.

      
Inspect the common query and selected result
The Python pipeline counts only records with an observed requested lifecycle. This browser filters the resulting source strata; it does not rerun the source adapters.
group eligible Learnlog capture records by source_id
where assistance.lifecycle.state == "observed"
  and assistance.lifecycle.value == "requested"
count recorded request observations
retain native request subtypes and unknown coverage
Inspect the full generated analysis and checks
The download includes mappings, source provenance and the reproducible analysis. These aggregate facts contain no raw dialogue or learner identifiers. Software checks establish the stated transformations, not independent methodological review.

A CAPTURE AGREEMENT IS A STARTING POINT
Keep the conditions
with the number.
Learnlog proposes assistance capture rules for existing logging ecosystems. Research still needs appropriate measures, populations, assistance conditions and study design.
Does Learnlog require a replacement event format?
The draft assistance capture profile supplies xAPI and Caliper bindings. The separate cross-source analysis uses candidate adapters into that profile. The interactive transformer also retains an earlier Learnlog record container for research excerpts; those earlier exports do not claim conformance to the new capture profile. The standalone container is an optional carrier with a separate justification.
Where do these data come from?
The source panel links each public research release, its license, the original file, the excerpt selection and file hashes. TutorMoments supplies released tutoring transcripts; OATutor supplies participant-level study data. The separate cross-source request analysis uses selected JetBrains Academy next-step hint and TutorTrace / IDETrace deployment-8 releases and publishes aggregate facts only. These are research releases, not current commercial-product exports.
Can I use my own data?
Yes, when its structure matches the selected source-specific adapter. The explicit assistance lifecycle adapter also accepts documented normalized assertions; its included sample is clearly synthetic and excluded from empirical measurements. Edited or unmatched uploads remain unverified. Only an exact match to the checked public excerpt receives its published-source attribution; a matching schema does not establish origin. Processing stays in this tab. Review both text and structured fields for identifying information before sharing outputs.
What does combining these data demonstrate?
The interval panel aggregates published scaffolding codes across two sessions from one provider, with every interval linked to source turns and judgments. The separate cross-source panel adds eligible request-record occurrences from different native formats and preserves source strata. In the interval panel, the second dataset exposes a measurement gap: assigned conditions do not supply comparable interval evidence. Turns and participants cannot be treated as comparable observations. Shared syntax does not establish equivalent measurement across products, learning effects or product rankings.

QLM TRANSFORMER
Mapping and research notes
The interactive transformer uses two public research excerpts with their original source structures. The separate cross-source request panel presents aggregate facts from its linked research releases. Source metadata and exact excerpt selection are visible beside each sample. The site makes no live product connection.
What travels with a record
The input-byte hash, mapping hash, original source locators and selected source fields travel with the generated records. The mapping states field treatment and exclusions. Hash consistency checks integrity; it does not independently authenticate the publisher or prove complete logging.
What the help evidence establishes
The transcript records student and tutor utterances, including real inquiries and tutor responses. Tutor turns are not automatically classified as scaffolding or successful help. Machine transcription may contain errors. The OATutor table records assigned help conditions and participant measures; it supplies no individual hint timeline. External help remains unobserved.
Designing a study with multiple sources
  1. Define the outcome, population and comparison before pooling data.
  2. Check what each source measures and what assistance it records.
  3. Preserve missingness and exclude incompatible measures explicitly.
  4. Collect additional event or assessment data where the question requires it.
The combined view is descriptive. Observation units and constructs remain source-specific. It supplies no causal effect estimate or performance ranking.
Privacy and pseudonyms
Processing uses browser-local code without analytics or persistent browser storage. The provided research releases contain publisher-de-identified records. Identifier pseudonymization does not anonymize free text. Pseudonyms are scoped to dataset, tenant and key. Records are not distinct-person counts; no cross-source identity linkage. Reloading creates a new pseudonym key; use only authorized inputs.
Learnlog is a draft assistance capture profile with xAPI and Caliper bindings. The existing research exports use a separate Learnlog container. This demo does not claim an adopted Internet Standard, certified interoperability or independent validation.
